name: Fragmentos, Espacio de Arte y Memoria
funding: Colombian Ministry of Culture space run by the Museo Nacional.
watch: In May 2021 President Duque held a political meeting in the space. Francis Alÿs withdrew his show and Doris Salcedo protested.
records_note: It sits under the Ministry of Culture and Museo Nacional.
affiliations_note: Fragmentos works with the Museo Nacional de Colombia, which links it in its main menu and takes its group visit bookings.

overview: Memorial, gallery and counter-monument at Carrera 7 # 6B-30 in La Candelaria, central Bogotá (stated by the space; Wikipedia).
Created by artist Doris Salcedo with architect Carlos Granada, chosen from 28 entries in an open competition. Opened on 10 December 2018 (Wikipedia; Radio Nacional).

The floor is 1,288 tiles cast from about 37 tons of steel melted from 8,994 weapons handed in by the FARC. Salcedo worked on the molds with 20 women who survived sexual violence in the conflict (Wikipedia).
Built among the ruins of an abandoned colonial-era house (Wikipedia).

From 2019 the Ministry of Culture and the Museo Nacional have held an annual call for artists' projects that answer the work. Shows have included Francis Alÿs (2020 to 2021), Beatriz González (2022 to 2023), Gabriela Golder (2023), Tania Candiani (2024) and Goya's "Los Desastres de la Guerra" (from 5 September 2026) (Wikipedia; Radio Nacional).
Visiting: Tuesday to Sunday, 9 am to 5 pm, closed Mondays, 1 January, 1 May and 25 December. Free entry and free programmes (stated by the space).
funding: The Government of Colombia, through the Ministry of Culture, sponsored and owns the site; the Museo Nacional de Colombia manages the gallery and its exhibitions (Wikipedia).

red_flags.heading: Protest over President Duque's use of the space (May 2021)
points: On 9 May 2021 President Iván Duque, members of his government and church leaders held a meeting in Fragmentos during the national strike, before the government opened talks with the strikers (El Universal).
Some of Francis Alÿs's works on show there were covered with white sheets (El Universal, 12 May 2021). Hyperallergic reported that Alÿs, the museum's board and Salcedo were not consulted.
Salcedo said the work had been "abusively used, breaking all the international norms of conservation and copyright", and of the meeting: "It was theater" (Hyperallergic).
Mexican curator Cuauhtémoc Medina published "El Museo Ocupado": "Así es como los gobernantes vampirizan la cultura" (El Universal).
El Universal reported that the episode led Alÿs to demand that his show be taken down.
The Ministry of Culture said "en ningún momento se rompió alguna norma" and the works "no presentan ninguna alteración" (El Universal, 14 May 2021).

press.overall: The criticism found is of the state's use of the space in 2021, not of Salcedo's work or the programme.

items.title: Valentina Di Liscia, "Colombian Government Exploited Doris Salcedo's Art to Denounce Nationwide Protests" (2021)
points: Argues the Duque government used a memorial to the conflict's victims as a stage while riot police met the protests with force; it cites dozens of deaths and at least 87 missing.
Quotes Salcedo's objection and notes that the Ministry of Culture did not respond.

items.title: Sonia Sierra, "'Gobernantes vampirizan la cultura'; cuestionan conversación del gobierno colombiano e iglesias en un museo" (2021)
points: Reports Medina's case that the space should serve reflection on the conflict's memory, not political ends, and that Alÿs was not asked.

items.title: Sonia Sierra, "Se protegió la obra de Francis Alÿs" (2021)
points: Not criticism: the Ministry of Culture's answer, which says the space was chosen for "su importancia simbólica" and that the work was protected with appropriate materials.

wider_context: During the 2021 national strike the state met protests over poverty, corruption and inequality with militarised riot police; the government called the protests "incitement of violence, hate, discord, and the destruction of society" (Hyperallergic).
Fragmentos is a Ministry of Culture site, and the government used it for its own meeting in the middle of that crackdown.
details.bottom_line: The only sponsor on record is the state: the Ministry of Culture owns and sponsored it and the Museo Nacional runs it, and no private sponsor was found. The weak point is control: in May 2021 the president used the memorial for a political meeting without consulting the artist. Worth watching: whether later governments use the space the same way.

name: Fototeca de Cuba
funding: Answers to the National Council of Plastic Arts (CNAP), a Ministry of Culture body. Opened in 1986 as a photo archive, museum and gallery.
watch: Runs the Noviembre Fotográfico month of photography since 2008 and offers creation and research grants to Cuban photographers.
records_note: A CNAP institution under the Ministry of Culture; its site, last archived 2022, gives its mission, history, publications and grant winners.
affiliations_note: Part of the National Council of Plastic Arts (CNAP), with the Centro de Arte Contemporáneo Wifredo Lam and the Centro de Desarrollo de las Artes Visuales.

overview: Photo archive, museum and gallery on Calle Mercaderes at Plaza Vieja in Old Havana (EcuRed).
Opened on 16 November 1986 to keep, study and promote the country's photographic heritage and to show international photography (EcuRed; CNAP).
Two galleries: María Eugenia Haya upstairs for established photographers, and Joaquín Blez on the ground floor for emerging ones. EcuRed says it holds about 16 exhibitions a year at its own address.
Runs the Coloquio de Fotografía from 2006, publishes the annual Revista de Fotografía Cubana FC from 2005, and offers a creation grant and a research grant to photographers living in Cuba (EcuRed).

Organises Noviembre Fotográfico, a month of photography across Havana. EcuRed dates it from 2008, and OnCuba (2012) says the Fototeca and CNAP have convened it every year since 2008. Radio Enciclopedia, relaying the state agency ACN, called the 2025 edition the 19th, and Prensa Latina did the same on 2025-11-04. Yearly editions from 2008 would make 2025 the 18th.
The 2025 edition was announced for 1 to 30 November under Fototeca director Lissette Solórzano, with venues beyond the Fototeca that included Fábrica de Arte Cubano and Factoría Habana (ACN claims).
Visiting: Artcrónica's directory lists Monday to Saturday, 9:00 to 17:00 (the listing is undated).
details.funding_verdict: Fototeca de Cuba: mainly public: Ministry of Culture through CNAP
funding: EcuRed says it answers to CNAP. CNAP, a Ministry of Culture body, lists the Fototeca among its institutions and Noviembre Fotográfico among its main events, organised by the Fototeca (archive copy of 2023-12-08).
details.bottom_line: The Fototeca is paid by the Cuban state through CNAP, and no flagged funder was found in the sources opened. The sources give different festival counts: a 2008 start in EcuRed and OnCuba, and a 19th edition in 2025 in Radio Enciclopedia and Prensa Latina. Worth watching: who funds Noviembre Fotográfico and the grants.

name: Muestra Joven ICAIC
funding: Screening of young Cuban directors' films run by ICAIC with a filmmakers' board. The 19th edition, set for April 2020, was postponed; 14ymedio wrote in 2025 that it had disappeared.
watch: 2018: ICAIC moved one film to a 24-seat room; the director withdrew it. 2020: ICAIC cut a documentary and at least six filmmakers withdrew works.
records_note: The Muestra's site publishes each edition's competition list, awards and poster contest.
affiliations_note: Run by ICAIC, which also runs the Cinemateca de Cuba and the Havana film festival.

overview: Film exhibition for young Cuban directors, held in April and sponsored by the Instituto Cubano del Arte e Industria Cinematográficos (ICAIC), according to the Muestra Joven site. Its board of directors includes filmmakers (OnCuba).

The competition covers fiction, documentary and animation by directors aged 35 or under, with a poster contest and "Haciendo Cine", a lab for low-budget projects that ends in a pitch to bodies that support production.
Havana Times, citing IPS Cuba, dates its start to 2001. The 18th edition ran in April 2019. ICAIC postponed the 19th, set for 7 to 12 April 2020, without a new date.
Havana Times published on 22 July 2025 a translation of a 14ymedio piece that says the Muestra has disappeared without explanation.
details.funding_verdict: Muestra Joven ICAIC: mainly public: Ministry of Culture, through ICAIC
funding: ICAIC, created in 1959, is a Ministry of Culture body (Wikipedia) and sponsors the event.

red_flags.heading: State censorship or punishment
points: 2018, 17th edition: ICAIC moved the work-in-progress film "Quiero hacer una película" by Yimit Ramírez to a 24-seat room, and he withdrew it. ICAIC's leadership told the press conference it would defend the institution's right to its own decisions (OnCuba). Havana Times states the film was pulled from the opening section on the claimed ground that it disrespected José Martí.

26 February 2020: the Muestra's board said ICAIC's presidency censored the documentary "Sueños al pairo" (José Luis Aparicio Ferrera and Fernando Fraguela Fosado, on the musician Mike Porcel) over political and ideological differences, after 13 days of dialogue (OnCuba, Havana Times). Aparicio told OnCuba that ICAIC objected to the film's treatment of the 1980 Mariel exodus.

28 February 2020: ICAIC replied that, as owner of the archive images, it refused their use in a montage whose context it does not share. It said this concerned the film's production and completion, not its screening at the Muestra, and that the film cannot be shown in Cuba or abroad (OnCuba).

Stated by the Muestra's board: ICAIC replaced its director Carla Valdés León with the institute's vice president, denied it control of its Facebook page and postponed the Muestra without consulting it (OnCuba).
Havana Times lists earlier removals in 2004, 2009 and 2011; after the last, the Muestra's director Fernando Pérez resigned over differences with ICAIC.

red_flags.heading: Protest or boycott
points: February 2020: at least six filmmakers withdrew works from the 19th edition in solidarity with the directors of "Sueños al pairo": Daniela Muñoz Barroso, Regis Guedes, Carla Valdés León, Carlos Lechuga (with Marcos Castillo), Josué García Gómez and Marcos Alejandro Yglesias Ravelo (OnCuba). The target was ICAIC's presidency.
The board condemned the censorship and asked for an assembly of filmmakers and institutions (OnCuba, Havana Times).

press.overall: News reporting and one column on the 2020 episode, from OnCuba, Havana Times and 14ymedio, an outlet critical of the government.

items.title: "Posponen Muestra Joven de cine. Realizadores retiran sus obras tras la censura de un documental" (2020)
points: Reports the removal of the documentary, the withdrawals and ICAIC's postponement, with the board's account that the presidency censored the film. Names ICAIC and its leadership.

items.title: "Icaic no autoriza uso de imágenes a documental censurado en Muestra Joven" (2020)
points: Sets ICAIC's copyright explanation beside the board's reply that political and ideological disagreement drove the decision.
Names ICAIC and its presidency.

items.title: IPS Cuba, "Youth Film Exhibition in Cuba Once Again Clouded in Controversy" (2020)
points: Places the dispute in a history of removed films and ties it to the lack of a film law. Names ICAIC.

items.title: Yoani Sánchez, "Mike Porcel, de censura en censura" (2020)
points: A column arguing that ICAIC's exclusion of the film and refusal of archive images repeat the silencing of Porcel in the 1980s. Names ICAIC.

wider_context: 14ymedio reported in January 2026 that the Assembly of Cuban Filmmakers rejected Resolution 61 of the Ministry of Culture and the Film Commission, which sets filming fees. The Assembly says it concentrates control in ICAIC and could work as indirect censorship.
details.bottom_line: The money is state money through ICAIC, and no flagged funder was found. The weak points are documented: ICAIC's 2018 relocation of a film, its 2020 removal of a documentary, the filmmakers' walkout and, per 14ymedio in 2025, the event's disappearance. Worth watching: whether ICAIC revives the Muestra and who governs it.

name: Museo Nacional de Artes Decorativas
funding: Directly subordinate to the National Council of Cultural Heritage (CNPC), a Ministry of Culture body. Opened 24 July 1964 in a mansion the state expropriated that year.
watch: Spanish Wikipedia says it holds over 33,000 works, including French furniture and Sèvres, Limoges and English porcelain.
records_note: Attached directly to the CNPC, the Ministry of Culture's heritage council, which names its director; its money is state heritage budget under Ley 155.
affiliations_note: One of five institutions directly subordinate to the National Council of Cultural Heritage (CNPC), with the Museo Ernest Hemingway.

overview: Decorative arts museum in a mansion at Calle 17 No. 502 in the Vedado (EcuRed).
Opened on 24 July 1964 (EcuRed; Spanish Wikipedia).

Building: the former home of María Luisa Gómez-Mena, widow of Cagiga and Countess of Revilla de Camargo, sister of José Gómez-Mena Vila, owner of the Manzana de Gómez. The Socarrás family bought it later, and the state expropriated it in 1964. Spanish Wikipedia gives this account and has carried a notice asking for references since April 2012.
Style: historicist, recalling French chateaux, with columns, wood, wrought iron and stairs of stone and Italian marble (Spanish Wikipedia).

Collection: EcuRed and Spanish Wikipedia claim over 33,000 works from the reigns of Louis XV, Louis XVI and Napoleon III, Asian pieces of the 16th to 20th centuries, and porcelain from Sèvres, Paris, Chantilly, Limoges, Derby, Chelsea, Wedgwood, Worcester and Staffordshire.
EcuRed and Spanish Wikipedia say a secretaire by Henri Riesener, once the personal furniture of Marie Antoinette at Versailles, is the main piece in the Neoclassical Salon.
details.funding_verdict: Museo Nacional de Artes Decorativas: mainly public: Ministry of Culture through the National Council of Cultural Heritage (CNPC)
funding: The CNPC is a Ministry of Culture body. Five institutions answer to it directly: the National Registry of Cultural Property, this museum, the Ernest Hemingway museum house, the National Dance Museum and the Servando Cabrera Moreno Museum-Library (Spanish Wikipedia, page edited 2026-08-28).
details.bottom_line: The museum is paid by the Cuban state through the Ministry of Culture's heritage council, and no flagged funder was found in the sources opened. The main weak point is thin sourcing: the building's history rests on a Spanish Wikipedia article that has asked for references since April 2012, and EcuRed carries the same collection text. Worth watching: the provenance of the collection.

name: Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de Cuba
funding: Under the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment (CITMA) since 1992, after 1985 to 1991 under the Ministry of Culture.
watch: Sits at Obispo 61 on Plaza de Armas in Old Havana. Its digital magazine Savia dates from February 2011.
records_note: Its site describes history, functions, collections and staff.
affiliations_note: Under the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment (CITMA), within its national science and technology system.

overview: National natural history museum at Calle Obispo 61, corner of Oficios, on the Plaza de Armas in Old Havana (museum site).

The museum's own history dates it to a 1959 project, the Museo Cubano de Ciencias Naturales. The project became the Museo de Ciencias "Felipe Poey" in 1962 to 1963, and in the stage from 1964 to 1980 its exhibitions opened to the public for the first time.

A restructuring from 1985 to 1991 turned it into the Museo Nacional de Historia Natural. The Capitolio was chosen as its home among the sites considered, and the history page marks a "new seat" stage from 1992 (museum site).
Spanish Wikipedia lists fossil, mammal, invertebrate and geology exhibits, among them a giant Cuban sloth skeleton and a moving replica of the planet.
The museum's research follows the rules of the national science and technology system under CITMA (museum site).
Its digital magazine Savia marked its seventh anniversary on 7 February 2018, so it began on 7 February 2011. Before 2011 it was a bulletin of the museum's teaching centre (museum site).

Visiting: a notice on the museum's site, archived 2022-01-20, announced a restart of public service from Friday to Sunday, 10:00 to 16:00. Reservations were preferred, and walk-in visits were accepted when there was capacity.
details.funding_verdict: Museo Nacional de Historia Natural: mainly public: Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment (CITMA)
funding: The museum's history page says it came under the Ministry of Culture in the 1985 to 1991 stage and, from the stage that starts in 1992, returned to the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment, where it remains. The archived sentence is garbled on this point.
details.bottom_line: The museum is paid by the Cuban state through CITMA, and no flagged funder was found in the sources opened. Worth watching: any published budget or donor data.

name: Cairo Opera House
funding: The page read does not state how the Cairo Opera House is funded.
watch: Home of the Egyptian ballet and opera company. In June 2013 its staff went on strike after the head of the opera house was dismissed by the culture minister.
records_note: No accounts were found in the pages read.

overview: The opera house in Cairo, home to the Egyptian ballet and opera company (Al Jazeera, 3 Jun 2013).
The pages read give no founding date, founder or building description.
What is there: the only company named in the page read is the Egyptian ballet and opera company; no repertoire or collection is described.
Archive: the page read describes none.
details.funding_verdict: Cairo Opera House: funder not stated in the page read
funding: No reporting found, in the page read, of grants, ministry budget or sponsors.

red_flags.heading: Labour dispute
points: Staff went on strike in 2013 after their boss was dismissed; Al Jazeera (3 Jun 2013) reports they accused President Mohamed Morsi's Muslim Brotherhood of trying to control cultural institutions, and that the opera house and other members of the artistic community demanded that Culture Minister Alaa Abdel Aziz resign. The page read gives no reply from the minister and no outcome.

details.bottom_line: The page read describes only a 2013 strike and no funding. The ministry's budget for the house and its current leadership remain to be established.

name: Museum of Modern Egyptian Art
funding: Owned by the Ministry of Culture.
highlight: Cairo's main modern art museum, in the former fair grounds of Zamalek, holds more than 13,000 paintings and sculptures.

overview: State art museum in Zamalek, Cairo, part of the National Cultural Centre on the former fair grounds of Zamalek (Wikipedia). Asharq Al-Awsat places it on Opera House Square.

Wikipedia gives its inauguration as 1927. Asharq Al-Awsat (Mohamed El-Kafrawy, 22 January 2025) reports that the museum has been in its current building since 1983, after its collection moved among several venues, mostly heritage palaces, and that it opened to the public in 1991 as one of the art venues of the Ministry of Culture, represented by the Fine Arts Sector.

Collection: more than 13,000 paintings and sculptures tracing Egyptian art from early 20th century pioneers to contemporary artists, including Mahmoud Said, Ragheb Ayad, Gazbia Sirry and Abdel Hadi Al-Gazzar (Wikipedia). Asharq Al-Awsat puts about 1,000 works on display and 16,000 to 18,000 in storage.

Closures: Asharq Al-Awsat reports that the museum was reopened in 2005, closed at times afterwards, reopened in 2020 and was then partly closed after the COVID-19 crisis and for development work. The works it lists include a permanent fix for ceiling leaks, central air conditioning, urgent maintenance including lighting and paint, updated security systems and an updated display layout, with a reopening show, "Khabiat Bikar", honouring the artist Hussein Bikar.
Visiting: from February 2025 the museum was set to open 9 am to 9 pm every day except Monday, and from 1 pm on Fridays (Asharq Al-Awsat).
details.funding_verdict: Museum of Modern Egyptian Art: mainly public: the Egyptian Ministry of Culture
funding: The Ministry of Culture owns the museum (Wikipedia) and runs it through the Fine Arts Sector (Asharq Al-Awsat).
details.bottom_line: The money behind the museum is the Egyptian state: the Ministry of Culture owns it and the Fine Arts Sector runs it.

name: HIAP (Helsinki International Artist Programme)
funding: Taike Arts Promotion Centre Finland, the Ministry of Education and Culture and the City of Helsinki are its main funders.
highlight: HIAP Gallery Augusta and the Suomenlinna residency studios are on Suomenlinna island.

overview: International artist residency and exhibition programme with its office, Gallery Augusta, a project space and residency studios on Suomenlinna island, and further studios on the fourth floor of the Cable Factory (Tallberginkatu 1) in Helsinki (hiap.fi/about).
Founded in 1998 by a coalition of Helsinki arts organisations. It runs as a non-profit association (hiap.fi/about).

Members of the association include Uniarts Helsinki's Academy of Fine Arts, Kunsthalle Helsinki, the Cable Factory, the Finnish Museum of Photography, Pixelache Festival, Zodiak Center for New Dance, Artists' Association MUU, AV-arkki, Gallery Huuto and Pro Artibus, plus one individual (hiap.fi/about).
Residencies last from 1 to 11 months for artists, curators and other cultural practitioners (hiap.fi/about).
The director is Emma Beverley. The board for 2026 to 2027 is chaired by Vappu Renko of the Cupore Center for Cultural Policy Research (hiap.fi/about).
HIAP Open Studios on Suomenlinna is on 31 October 2026, 15:00 to 20:00 (hiap.fi).
details.funding_verdict: HIAP: public funders: Taike (Arts Promotion Centre Finland), the Ministry of Education and Culture and the City of Helsinki
funding: HIAP names Taike Arts Promotion Centre Finland, the Ministry of Education and Culture and the City of Helsinki as its main funders (hiap.fi/about).
details.bottom_line: The money behind HIAP is Finnish public funding: Taike, the Ministry of Education and Culture and the City of Helsinki, which HIAP names as its main funders (stated by HIAP).

name: Kunsthalle Tbilisi
funding: Roving space founded 2018 by Irena Popiashvili and Lika Chkuaseli; mostly private donors with a small municipal share (unnamed).
watch: No donors are named on its site.
records_note: Its archived site has one About paragraph naming two founders.

overview: Non-profit contemporary art initiative in Tbilisi without a permanent building, led by the curators Irena Popiashvili and Lika Chkuaseli (The Art Newspaper, 16 May 2018). Its own site describes it as a roving exhibition space founded by the two curators, showing Georgian and international art in locations across Tbilisi (archived February 2023).

Launched on 18 May 2018 with two solo shows: Nika Kutateladze in a Soviet studio apartment on Pavlov Street and Angelica Mesiti in a winery on Petriashvili Street (The Art Newspaper, Lorena Muñoz-Alonso, 16 May 2018).
The Art Newspaper calls it "the nomadic project Kunsthalle Tbilisi" and describes it as chief among the initiatives supporting education and local artists in the city (23 May 2018).

In 2024 it used a rented apartment as a venue: "Conspiracy Bar" by the collective Around the Studio ran from 27 September to 7 November 2024 in a rented apartment, with video and film screenings, music and experimental theatre (Kunsthalle Tbilisi site, archived July 2025).
Visiting: for that exhibition, Thursday to Sunday 14:00 to 19:00 and by appointment.
details.funding_verdict: Kunsthalle Tbilisi: private non-profit, per The Art Newspaper
funding: The Art Newspaper (23 May 2018) writes that in Tbilisi "commercial galleries, art fairs and privately funded non-profits" step in, and calls Kunsthalle Tbilisi chief among these initiatives.
details.bottom_line: Kunsthalle Tbilisi is a non-profit that works in changing venues, including a rented apartment in 2024, led by its two founding curators. The Art Newspaper's article of 23 May 2018 places it among the commercial galleries, art fairs and privately funded non-profits of Tbilisi.

name: Bauhaus-Archiv / Museum für Gestaltung
funding: The pages read did not state who funds the Bauhaus-Archiv or give amounts. The Gropius building is being renovated and extended by Staab Architekten; a Berlin development site reported on 9 February 2026 that completion had moved from autumn 2025 to the end of 2026, with public opening in 2027.
watch: The main building on Klingelhöferstraße is closed; the museum shows its work at the Temporary Bauhaus-Archiv and calls itself the owner of the world's largest Bauhaus collection. Brigitte Franzen became director in April 2026 (Entwicklungsstadt, 9 February 2026).
records_note: The pages read gave no accounts.

overview: The Bauhaus-Archiv / Museum für Gestaltung is a museum and archive of the Bauhaus (1919 to 1933) in Berlin; its Gropius-designed building is closed for renovation and an extension by Staab Architekten (museum website).
Founder and opening year: the pages read did not state them.
What is there: the museum describes its holding as 'the world's largest collection on the Bauhaus (1919 to 1933)'; the pages read gave no object count (museum website).
Archive: the site has a Research section; the pages read gave no figures for the archive or library (museum website).
While the main building is closed the museum shows its work at the Temporary Bauhaus-Archiv; the exhibition 'One Million Objects' runs from 14 October 2026 to 30 April 2027 (museum website).
details.funding_verdict: Bauhaus-Archiv: funding not stated on the pages read; a publicly visible construction project
funding: No reporting found of the museum's funders, annual budget or construction cost on the pages read.

red_flags.heading: Building delay
points: Completion of the renovation and new building was earlier communicated for autumn 2025; Entwicklungsstadt reported on 9 February 2026 that the new target is the end of 2026 with public opening in 2027, more than two years behind the last expected timeframe.

Brigitte Franzen, director from April 2026, told the Tagesspiegel in an interview, as relayed by Entwicklungsstadt, that the project is delayed again and that the closure is a chance to reach new audiences.
No reporting found of a row over the directorship on the pages read.

details.bottom_line: The pages read give no funder or cost figures, so the money cannot be traced from them. The reported issue is the repeated delay of the reopening.
